report.title: Fuzz case: boundary-001
report.subtitle: One confirmed bug from the E.3 adversarial campaign
report.summary: A BOM-prefixed frontmatter template reproduced a stable output leak across three runs.

sections.title: boundary-001
sections.context_text: Campaign e3-20260729-0002; boundary-probe; confirmed finding boundary-001. A BOM-prefixed frontmatter document leaked its frontmatter block into rendered output in 3 reproductions.

json_payload.minimal_template:
UTF-8 bytes EF BB BF followed by ---
variables:
  name:
    required: false
---
Hello {{name}}
json_payload.expected_oracle: UTF-8 BOM is accepted before frontmatter; output contains only the rendered body
json_payload.observed_result: exit 0; stdout includes the complete frontmatter block before Hello x
json_payload.recommended_test: Add a CLI regression test for BOM-prefixed frontmatter parsing.

sections.requirement_trace: No requirement or ADR currently covers this BOM-frontmatter behavior; the campaign applied the parser boundary oracle recorded in the E.3 evidence.
sections.root_cause: The file-frontmatter path does not strip the leading UTF-8 BOM before detecting the frontmatter delimiter, so the delimiter is rendered as ordinary template content.
sections.requirement_follow_up: Assess whether BOM-prefixed frontmatter is a supported user contract. If yes, create or update the requirement/ADR before implementing the parser fix; if no, document the intentional boundary rather than creating a needless ADR.
sections.recommended_fix: Add a CLI regression test for BOM-prefixed frontmatter parsing, then implement the requirement/ADR decision above and normalize a leading UTF-8 BOM if the behavior is supported.

recommendations: Do not create an ADR solely because the finding lacks a reference; first decide whether the behavior is a supported contract and whether the gap is genuine.
